### Health Analytics with R · Module 02: EDA in Healthcare
***
**Learning objectives**
- Visualise missing data patterns with `naniar`
- Test MCAR, MAR, and MNAR mechanisms with statistical tests
- Apply median, LOCF, and multiple imputation (MICE) strategies
- Compare imputed vs original distributions with overlapping KDE plots
- Document imputation decisions for a reproducible analysis plan

**Estimated time:** 2 hours | **Level:** Intermediate | **Libraries:** `dplyr` / tibble, naniar, visdat, `mice`, ggplot2

## 1. Setup & Dataset with Realistic Missingness


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# install.packages(c("naniar", "visdat", "mice"))
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(naniar)
library(visdat)
library(mice)
library(patchwork)

mod02_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod02")
dir.create(mod02_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

theme_health <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
    )
}
theme_set(theme_health())

cat("naniar imported successfully.\n")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
naniar imported successfully.
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# ── Base dataset ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 800
ages     <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes    <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers   <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                   N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges  <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
set.seed(99)
df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  los_days      = los_days,
  diabetes      = rbinom(N, 1, 0.32),
  hypertension  = rbinom(N, 1, 0.45),
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14),
  total_charge  = charges
)

# ── Introduce structured missingness (realistic clinical patterns) ─────────────
set.seed(7)

# MCAR — completely random (8% glucose)
df$glucose <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 105, 28), 50), 400), 1)
df$glucose[runif(N) < 0.08] <- NA_real_

# MAR — missing more often in Self-pay (lab deferral due to cost)
df$creatinine <- round(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 1.6, scale = 0.6), 0.4), 10), 2)
selfpay_mask <- df$payer == "Self-pay"
df$creatinine[selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.55)] <- NA_real_
df$creatinine[!selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.10)] <- NA_real_

# MNAR — HbA1c missing more often when values are in normal range (not ordered)
df$hba1c <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 6.8, 1.4), 4), 14), 1)
low_hba1c <- df$hba1c < 5.7
df$hba1c[low_hba1c & (runif(N) < 0.60)] <- NA_real_
df$hba1c[!low_hba1c & (runif(N) < 0.15)] <- NA_real_

# Charge missing correlated with Self-pay
df$total_charge <- charges
df$total_charge[selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.40)] <- NA_real_
df$total_charge[!selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.05)] <- NA_real_

cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))
```

## 4. Imputation Strategies


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Store complete-case subsets for comparison
glucose_complete <- df$glucose[!is.na(df$glucose)]

# ── 4.1  Median imputation (simple, robust to outliers) ─────────────────────
df$glucose_median <- naniar::impute_median(df$glucose)
cat(sprintf("Median imputed: %d NaN → 0\n", sum(is.na(df$glucose))))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Median imputed: 74 NaN → 0
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# ── 4.2  LOCF — Last Observation Carried Forward (longitudinal data) ─────────
# Simulate a longitudinal HbA1c series for 50 patients over 4 quarters
set.seed(55)
n_pts <- 50
n_periods <- 4
long_df <- tibble(
  patient_id = rep(sprintf("PT-%03d", seq_len(n_pts)), each = n_periods),
  quarter    = rep(seq_len(n_periods) - 1L, times = n_pts),
  hba1c      = round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pts * n_periods, 6.8, 1.2), 4), 13), 1)
)
# Introduce 25% missingness
long_df$hba1c[runif(nrow(long_df)) < 0.25] <- NA_real_
long_df <- long_df %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  arrange(quarter, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  fill(hba1c, .direction = "down") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(hba1c_locf = hba1c)
n_still_missing <- sum(is.na(long_df$hba1c_locf))
cat(sprintf("\nLOCF — residual missing after forward fill: %d\n", n_still_missing))
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# ── 4.3  KNN Imputation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
num_cols <- c("age", "los_days", "glucose", "creatinine", "hba1c", "total_charge")
df_num   <- df %>% select(all_of(num_cols))

knn_impute <- function(dat, k = 5) {
  x <- as.matrix(dat)
  mus <- apply(x, 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  sds <- apply(x, 2, sd,   na.rm = TRUE)
  sds[sds == 0 | is.na(sds)] <- 1
  xs <- sweep(sweep(x, 2, mus, "-"), 2, sds, "/")
  xs_fill <- xs
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(xs_fill))) {
    xs_fill[is.na(xs_fill[, j]), j] <- 0
  }
  miss <- which(is.na(x), arr.ind = TRUE)
  out <- x
  for (i in unique(miss[, 1])) {
    cols_miss <- miss[miss[, 1] == i, 2, drop = TRUE]
    d <- sqrt(rowSums((xs_fill -
                         matrix(xs_fill[i, ], nrow = nrow(xs_fill),
                                ncol = ncol(xs_fill), byrow = TRUE))^2))
    d[i] <- Inf
    nn <- order(d)[seq_len(min(k, length(d) - 1))]
    w  <- 1 / pmax(d[nn], 1e-8)
    w  <- w / sum(w)
    for (j in cols_miss) {
      out[i, j] <- sum(w * (xs_fill[nn, j] * sds[j] + mus[j]))
    }
  }
  as.data.frame(out)
}

df_knn <- knn_impute(df_num, k = 5)
cat("KNN imputation complete.\n")
```

## 5. Comparing Imputed Distributions


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_kde_compare <- function(col, title) {
  orig <- tibble(value = df[[col]], source = "Original (complete cases)") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value))
  knn  <- tibble(value = df_knn[[col]], source = "KNN imputed")
  mice <- tibble(value = df_mice[[col]], source = "MICE imputed")
  bind_rows(orig, knn, mice) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = value, colour = source, linetype = source)) +
    geom_density(linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "Original (complete cases)" = "black",
      "KNN imputed"  = "#2563EB",
      "MICE imputed" = "#DC2626"
    )) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
      "Original (complete cases)" = "solid",
      "KNN imputed"  = "dashed",
      "MICE imputed" = "dotted"
    )) +
    labs(title = title, y = "Density", x = NULL, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
    theme_health() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
}

p_cmp <- plot_kde_compare("glucose", "Glucose (mg/dL)") +
  plot_kde_compare("creatinine", "Creatinine (mg/dL)") +
  plot_kde_compare("hba1c", "HbA1c (%)") +
  plot_annotation(title = "Distribution comparison — original vs imputation strategies")
print(p_cmp)
```

## 6. Imputation Decision Framework


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
decision_rules <- tibble(
  Variable = c("glucose", "creatinine", "hba1c", "total_charge"),
  Mechanism = c("MCAR", "MAR (by payer)", "MNAR (missing when normal)", "MAR (by payer)"),
  pct_miss = c(8, 18, 35, 12),
  chosen = c(
    "KNN (preserves multivariate relationships)",
    "MICE with payer as predictor",
    "MICE + sensitivity analysis with worst-case scenario",
    "MICE on log(charge), back-transform to original scale"
  )
)
```

## 7. Knowledge Check
1. What is the key difference between MCAR and MAR? Why does it matter for imputation?
2. Why should you NOT use LOCF for a cross-sectional dataset?
3. MICE ran 10 iterations. How would you check if it converged?
4. HbA1c has 35% MNAR missingness. Why might any imputation method produce biased estimates?
5. Re-run KNN imputation with `k = 10`. Do the distributions change materially?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

  tibble(value = df_knn$glucose,  source = "KNN k=5"),
```
